column5: ReturnSheet at src/views/OrderDetailView/ReturnSheet.tsx is the return request UI actually mounted - src/views/OrderDetailView/index.tsx:681 renders it. Its file handler at :67-68 reads Array.from(e.target.files ?? []) and does setImages(prev => [...prev - ...files].slice(0 - 5)) - so the ONLY constraint applied is a count cap of five. There is no file.type check and no file.size check. The accept="image/*" attribute at :192 is a file picker hint and not validation - a caller can select any file by changing the dialog filter and a scripted submit ignores it entirely. The files are then posted through returnOrderItem which appends them as images[] in a multipart body (src/services/orders.ts:70-117). The component this replaced still exists and shows what the validation used to be: ReturnOrderItemModal enforces a five image cap at :309 - rejects anything failing file.type.startsWith('image/') at :320 - and rejects files above a 5MB MAX_IMAGE_SIZE at :42 and :329. That modal is no longer rendered anywhere in src so the validated path is dead and the unvalidated one is live. This is a regression introduced by the redesign rather than a gap that was always there.

column15: Storage and bandwidth abuse from oversized uploads on an authenticated endpoint - and if the panel stores and later serves these files inline a non-image such as an SVG becomes a stored injection vector. That compounds code review issue 38 which records that the storefront sanitises no API supplied HTML and code review issue 3 which records that there is no Content-Security-Policy to contain it.
